title: Open questions in gut sensing
objective: Name current open questions in spinal visceral sensation and why they matter.

steps.title: What we still don't know
steps.body:
The 2025 review flags open questions for spinal ([[DRG]]) gut sensing, including:

- Do more subtypes exist **beyond the colon** (stomach, small intestine, other organs)?
- What are their **central (dorsal-horn) projection patterns**?
- How does the **microbiome** shape these neurons?
- Do afferents form true **synapses** with [[enterochromaffin cell|enterochromaffin cells]], or just sit close?

steps.prompt: Why is 'beyond the colon' an open question at all?
options: Most DRG-subtype mapping so far has focused on the distal colon
Organs above the colon are innervated only by the vagus, not by DRG
DRG neurons outside the colon have no marker genes to target
Colon subtypes are already known to be the same in every organ
steps.explanation: The genetic subtype story has been built mainly in the distal colon; whether the same or new subtypes serve the stomach, small intestine, or pancreas is largely untested — which is where new projects come in.

variants.setup: DRG subtype work has centered on the distal colon.
variants.prompt: Why is extending to other organs open?
options: Other organs aren't yet mapped this way
Other organs are innervated only by the vagus
Colon subtypes are known to be identical elsewhere
variants.reveal: The subtype map is colon-centric; other organs are largely uncharted.

steps.setup: Evidence conflicts on whether gut afferents truly synapse with EC cells or merely lie nearby.
options: A true synapse means fast, specific signaling; proximity means slow, diffuse signaling
Only a true synapse would let serotonin act as the messenger here
Without a synapse, the signal would have to travel in the bloodstream
Only a true synapse can be confirmed by electron microscopy
steps.reveal: A dedicated synapse supports rapid, targeted transmission; diffusion across a gap is slower and less specific. Which one it is changes how we model gut chemosensation — an unsettled, actively-studied point.

variants.prompt: Whether EC cell–afferent contact is a true synapse matters because…
options: It changes whether signaling is fast/specific vs slow/diffuse
Only a synapse would let serotonin act as the messenger
Without a synapse the signal must travel in the blood
variants.explanation: Synapse vs proximity changes the speed and specificity of the signal.
